title: Home
h1b_desc: For workers in specialty occupations like tech, engineering, and finance. Requires a US employer sponsor. Valid for 3 years, extendable to 6
h2a_desc: For temporary agricultural workers. Allows foreign nationals to work on US farms during peak seasons.
l1_desc: For employees transferring within the same company from a foreign office to a US office. Requires at least 1 year of employment
f1_desc: For full-time academic students at accredited US colleges or universities. Allows limited on-campus work and OPT after graduation
j1_desc: For exchange visitors including students, interns, teachers, and researchers in approved programs
m1_desc: For vocational and non-academic students. Covers trade schools, culinary programs, and flight academies
b2_desc: For tourism, vacation, visiting family, or medical treatment. Typically allows a stay of up to 6 months
b1_desc: For business visitors attending meetings or conferences. Does not allow you to work for a US employer
esta_desc: Citizens of 40+ countries can visit the US for up to 90 days without a visa. Must apply online before travel
family_desc: For immediate relatives of US citizens including spouses, unmarried children under 21, and parents
workgc_desc: For workers with job offers from US employers. Divided into preference categories EB-1 through EB-5
refugee_desc: Refugees and asylees who have been in the US for at least one year may apply for permanent residency
lottery_desc: Each year 55,000 green cards are available through a random lottery to people from countries with low US immigration rates
e1_title: If ICE Comes to Your Door
e1_body: Do not open the door. Ask if they have a judicial warrant signed by a judge. An administrative warrant does not give them the right to enter your home
e2_body: You do not have to answer any questions. Clearly say: "I am exercising my right to remain silent." This applies to everyone regardless of immigration status
e3_body: You have the right to speak with a lawyer. Do not sign any documents before speaking to one. Ask for a free legal aid organization if you cannot afford one
e4_body: Stay calm and keep your hands visible. You are not required to answer questions about your immigration status
offices_desc: Find immigration offices and legal aid organizations near you
h1b_doverview: The H-1B visa allows US companies to employ foreign workers in technology, engineering, finance, and other specialized fields
h1b_dphrase: "Requires a higher education degree or its equivalent"
h1b_dreq1: A valid job offer from a US company
h1b_dreq2: A university degree in your specific field
h1b_dreq3: The employer must file a Labor Condition Application
h2a_doverview: The H-2A visa brings foreign nationals to the US to fill temporary or seasonal agricultural jobs where local workers are unavailable
h2a_dben1: The employer must provide free housing to workers
h2a_dben3: Generally valid for up to 1 year (extendable to 3)
l1_doverview: For managers, executives, or employees with specialized knowledge transferring to a US branch of the same company
l1_dreq1: Must have worked for the company abroad for at least 1 continuous year within the last 3 years
l1_dreq2: L-1A (Managers/Executives) can stay up to 7 years
l1_dreq3: L-1B (Specialized Knowledge) can stay up to 5 years
f1_doverview: The F-1 visa is for international students who want to study full-time at an accredited college or university in the US
f1_dphrase: "Must maintain a full course of study"
f1_dwork1: On-Campus Work: Up to 20 hours per week while classes are in session
f1_dwork2: OPT: Up to 12 months of temporary work in your field after graduation
j1_doverview: For individuals approved to participate in work-and-study exchange visitor programs (interns, scholars, au pairs, camp counselors)
j1_dnote: Some J-1 visas include a 2-year home-country physical presence requirement before you can change your status inside the US
m1_doverview: For students attending non-academic or vocational programs, such as technical schools, flight academies, or trade courses
m1_dlim1: M-1 students cannot work off-campus during their studies
m1_dlim2: Visas are generally issued for the duration of the program, up to a maximum of 1 year
b2_doverview: For travelers entering the US for tourism, vacation, visiting friends or family, and medical treatments
b2_dstay: Generally grants a stay period of up to 6 months per trip, decided by CBP customs officers at the border
b1_doverview: For short-term business travel to consult with associates, attend legal conventions, negotiate contracts, or settle estates
b1_dphrase: "Strictly prohibits local employment or receiving payment from US sources"
esta_doverview: Allows pre-approved citizens of over 40 specific countries to travel to the US for business or tourism without a traditional visa
esta_drule1: Maximum stay limit of 90 days per visit
esta_drule2: Strictly non-extendable while inside the country
esta_drule3: Must register online before booking travel
family_doverview: Allows the sponsorship of lawful permanent residency for relatives of US citizens and Green Card holders
family_dcat1: Immediate Relatives: Spouses, minor children, parents (No annual limits or waitlists)
family_dcat2: Family Preference: Siblings, married or adult children (Subject to backlogs due to annual caps)
workgc_doverview: Permanent residency pathways based on professional skills, job offers, or commercial investments within the United States
workgc_dtier2: EB-2: Advanced degrees or exceptional professional abilities
refugee_doverview: For individuals seeking legal protection who are unable or afraid to return to their home country due to a well-founded fear of persecution
refugee_drule: Refugees and asylees are legally required or entitled to apply for a Green Card after living continuously in the U.S. for exactly 1 year
lottery_doverview: An official, computer-generated random drawing program that awards up to 55,000 permanent resident visas every year
lottery_delig: Open only to natives of countries with historically low rates of immigration to the United States. Requires a high school education or equivalent work history
back_to_home: Go back to the home screen
back_to_tourist_visa: Return to business and tourist visa list
